title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 39
paragraphs: At Sparta, Anaxandrides, son of Leon, was no longer alive as king, but had come to the end of his life; and Cleomenes, son of Anaxandrides, held the royal power, not having obtained it by merit but by right of birth. For Anaxandrides had as wife his own sister's daughter, whom he loved dearly, but no children were born to him by her. This being so, the Ephors summoned him before them and said: “If you will not take thought for yourself in time, yet we cannot allow this to happen—that the race of Eurysthenes should become extinct. Therefore set aside the wife you now have, since, as you know, she bears you no children, and marry another; and in doing so you will please the Spartans.” He answered that he would do neither of these two things, and that they were not giving him honorable counsel in advising him to send away the wife he had—who had done him no wrong—and take another into his house; in short, he would not follow their advice.
